'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**An explosion at a religious gathering during a [[Quran]] recitation ceremony in [[Ghazni]], [[Afghanistan]], has killed at least 15 civilians and wounded 20 others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/12/18/explosion-in-central-afghanistan-kills-at-least-15-official (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Seven civilians and three soldiers are killed after a [[suicide bomber]] [[detonate]]s his device outside a stadium in [[Galkayo]], [[Mudug]]. [[Prime Minister of Somalia|Prime Minister]] [[Mohamed Hussein Roble]] was due to address a gathering at the stadium. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-12/19/c_139603154.htm (Xinhua)]
*[[Tigray conflict]]
**[[Ethiopia]] offers a reward of 10 million [[Ethiopian birr|birr]] (about [[United States dollar|US$]]250,000) for information leading to the capture of [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] officials, including leader [[Debretsion Gebremichael]], who are currently in hiding following the [[Mekelle offensive (2020)|fall of]] [[Mekelle]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20201218-ethiopia-offers-reward-for-help-finding-dissident-tigray-leaders (France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)|War in Afghanistan]]
**An explosion kills 15 children and injures another 20 people in [[Ghazni]], [[Afghanistan]], after a piece of [[unexploded ordnance]] blows up when the children try to sell it to a vendor. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-55372281 (BBC News)]

****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Minnesota]]
*****[[Minnesota Senate|Minnesota Senator]] [[Jerry Relph]] dies from COVID-19 complications. [https://apnews.com/article/st-cloud-coronavirus-pandemic-minnesota-68883302ba65345909b7bb2339a642d1 (AP)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****[[New York (state)|New York]] reports a record 12,697 new cases in the past 24 hours, surpassing the previous record set in April. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-12-18/n-y-new-covid-19-cases-top-12-000-most-since-pandemic-began (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico City]] and the [[State of Mexico]] move back to the "red traffic light". All non-essential activity will be suspended until January 10 due to an "alarming" increase in both infections and hospital occupancies. [https://www.milenio.com/politica/semaforo-rojo-cdmx-edomex-regresan-covid19 (''Milenio'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Austria]]
****[[Chancellor of Austria|Chancellor]] [[Sebastian Kurz]] announces that the [[Austria|country]] will impose a third nationwide [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns|lockdown]] beginning on December 26. However, people who take part in mass testing programmes between January 15 and 17 and test negative will be allowed to enter shops and restaurants beginning on January 18. [https://www.barrons.com/articles/austria-to-enter-third-virus-lockdown-from-december-26-01608312011 (''Barron's'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy]]
****[[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Giuseppe Conte]] announces a second nationwide "red zone" [[lockdown]] from December 24–27, December 31–January 3, and January 5–6. On those days, people will only be allowed to travel for work, health or emergency reasons. An "orange zone", where shops are allowed to open, will be in effect from December 28–30 and on January 4. However, all bars and restaurants will remain closed during the holiday season. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-italy-christmas/italy-govt-orders-christmas-new-year-lockdown-to-prevent-covid-surge-idUSKBN28S2Y2 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Croatia]]
****[[Ministry of the Interior (Croatia)|Interior Minister]] [[Davor Božinović]] announces that [[Croatia]] will impose a ban on travel outside one's [[Counties of Croatia|county]] between December 23 and January 8. [https://www.croatiaweek.com/croatia-imposes-ban-on-travel-outside-counties-from-23-dec-to-8-jan/ (Croatia Week)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Burundi]]
****Former [[President of Burundi]] [[Pierre Buyoya]] dies from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] at a hospital in [[Paris]], [[France]]. [https://www.macaubusiness.com/burundi-ex-president-buyoya-dies-from-covid-19/ (Macau Business)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Germany]] reports a record 33,777 new cases in the past 24 hours, according to data from the [[Robert Koch Institute]], bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,439,938. [https://www.bild.de/ratgeber/2020/ratgeber/aktuelle-daten-corona-zahlen-rki-meldet-33777-neuinfektionen-813-tote-73511706.bild.html (''Bild'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovakia]]
****[[Prime Minister of Slovakia|Prime Minister]] [[Igor Matovič]] tests positive for COVID-19. [https://spectator.sme.sk/c/22558189/slovak-pm-matovic-covid-positive.html (''The Slovak Spectator'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Ministry of Health (Spain)|Health Minister]] [[Salvador Illa]] announces that the nationwide [[vaccination]] campaign will begin on December 27. [https://www.rtve.es/noticias/20201218/vacuna-espana-salvador-illa-ministerio-sanidad/2060548.shtml (RTVE)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sweden]]
****[[Prime Minister of Sweden|Prime Minister]] [[Stefan Löfven]] announces new measures to reduce the second wave of the pandemic. All non-essential public services will close until January 24, alcohol sales will be banned after 8:00 p.m. local time, and the number of people at restaurants will be limited to four per table. It also recommended to use [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|face mask]]s on public transport at certain times. [https://www.thelocal.se/20201218/swedish-prime-minister-stefan-lofven-press-conference-coronavirus (The Local Sweden)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland]]
****The [[Government of Switzerland|Swiss government]] announces that restaurants, bars and  sports and leisure centres, as well as libraries, museums and other cultural institutions will close on December 22 to help reduce the spread of COVID-19 as the total numbers of cases and deaths surpass 400,000 and 6,000 respectively. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/new-anti-corona-measures--restaurants-closed--ski-areas-open/46232960 (Swiss Info)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nigeria]]
****The [[Government of Lagos State|Lagos State Government]] orders all public and private schools in the [[Lagos State|state]] to close until further notice. The government also recommends that all [[public servant]]s from Grade Level 14 and below, except emergency workers and first responders, work from home for 14 days beginning December 21. [https://nairametrics.com/2020/12/18/breaking-lagos-shuts-public-private-schools-indefinitely-civil-servants-to-work-remotely/ (Nairametrics)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[South Africa]] surpasses 900,000 total cases of COVID-19. [https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2020-12-18-sa-surges-past-900000-confirmed-covid-19-cases-with-8700-in-24-hours/ (TimesLive)]
****[[501.V2 Variant]]
*****[[Minister of Health (South Africa)|Health Minister]] [[Zweli Mkhize]] announces the discovery of a severe variant of [[SARS-CoV-2]], named 501.V2, which contributed to the second wave of COVID-19 in the country. [https://www.iol.co.za/news/politics/sa-experiencing-a-new-covid-19-variant-health-minister-d16e1fe8-dfd1-5419-b10d-916d9437f17b (Independent Online)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****The total number of confirmed COVID-19 cases in Malaysia surpasses 90,000. [https://www.themalaysianinsight.com/s/290646 (The Malaysian Insight)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports 2,122 new cases, the highest daily total in more than a month, bringing the nationwide total to 456,562 cases. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/12/18/20/ph-reports-2122-new-covid-19-cases-highest-tally-in-over-a-month (ABS-CBN News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Panama]]
***Starting from December 21, [[Panama]] will reimpose nationwide restrictions by require men and women to carry out holiday shopping on different days. On [[Christmas]] and [[New Year's Day]] there will be total lockdown for all genders. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/panama-orders-men-and-women-to-shop-on-different-days-to-curb-coronavirus (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]]
**[[George Floyd protests]], [[George Floyd protests in New York City]]
***The [[New York City Department of Investigation]] accuses the [[New York City Police Department|police department]] of mishandling their response to [[Black Lives Matter]] protests in the [[New York City|city]], which broke out following the [[Killing of George Floyd|killing]] of [[George Floyd]]. [https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/nypd-faulted-in-handling-of-george-floyd-protests-11608307527 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**[[Aristóteles Sandoval]], former [[Governor of Jalisco]], [[Mexico]], is killed in an attack in [[Puerto Vallarta]]. Current Governor [[Enrique Alfaro Ramírez]] said that Sandoval was the victim of a "direct attack". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mexico-crime/former-mexican-governor-of-jalisco-killed-in-attack-idUSKBN28S1PY?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Islamic Defenders Front]], [[Islam in Indonesia]]
**Supporters of the controversial [[Indonesia|Indonesian]] [[Ulama|Islamic cleric]] [[Muhammad Rizieq Shihab]] clash with [[Indonesian National Police|police]] during a [[Demonstration (political)|demonstration]] in [[Jakarta]], demanding immediate release of Shihab from police detention. Shihab was arrested last weekend for violations of [[Pandemic prevention|health protocols]] during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] after large gatherings occurred to celebrate his return to the country from [[Exile|self-exile]] in [[Saudi Arabia]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-indonesia-security-islamist-protest/supporters-of-hardline-indonesian-cleric-clash-with-police-in-jakarta-idUKKBN28S17N (Reuters)]
*The [[Supreme Court of the United States]], in an unsigned 6–3 decision, dismisses ''[[Trump v. New York]]'', ruling that the challenge to the Trump administration's memo requiring the [[United States Census Bureau|Census Bureau]] to report the results of the [[2020 United States census]] with the exclusion of [[undocumented immigrant]]s for apportionment is premature, and that no judicial review can be taken until after the data has been collected. The Bureau faces a December 31 deadline to report the results, which they have previously indicated that they may miss. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/18/us/supreme-court-census.html (''The New York Times'')]

*[[LGBT rights in Switzerland]]
**[[Switzerland]] [[Recognition of same-sex unions in Switzerland|legalizes same-sex marriage]] and for people to change their gender on official documents, pending an expected referendum challenging the law. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-switzerland-lgbt-lawmaking-trfn/switzerland-votes-for-same-sex-marriage-easing-legal-gender-change-idUSKBN28S2T5 (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2020 United States federal government data breach]]
**The [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]] confirms that it has been [[Data breach|breached]] along with other [[Federal government of the United States|federal government agencies]], but says that the country's [[nuclear weapon]]s arsenal has not been compromised. The mass data breach is now considered the worst ever [[cyberattack]] on the [[U.S. government]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-55358332 (BBC)]
*A review of some recent medical studies shows that [[memory T cells]] may play a role in a phenomenon known as [[cross-reactivity]], which researchers found may perhaps give certain people, in some cases, some level of immunity to the virus that causes [[COVID-19]] even without them having been exposed to or infected with the virus, or having received a vaccine. There are certain structural and clinical similarities between the virus that causes COVID-19 and the other coronaviruses that are related to it, which cause [[SARS]] and [[MERS]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/health/medical/some-people-may-have-preexisting-immunity-to-the-coronavirus/ar-BB1c1Ftr (MSN)] 
*The [[British Antarctic Survey]] confirms that [[Iceberg A-68]], one of the [[List of recorded icebergs by area|largest ever recorded icebergs]] with a surface area of 5,800 square kilometres, has broken in two in the [[South Atlantic]] as it approaches [[South Georgia (island)|South Georgia]] island. The new smaller iceberg has been named A68D. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/dec/18/massive (''The Guardian'')]
